sourceInformation.source: Demon Attack (1982), Imagic; Rob Fulop. Original interpretation; no source assets.
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 WebGPURenderer (WebGPU, WebGL compatibility fallback); Rapier 0.19.3; Web Audio; Gamepad API; AI Hub session client 1.4.0; optional PeerJS 1.5.5; bundled with esbuild 0.28.2
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded / ink illustration: faceted paper-wing demons, heavy outlines, icy crags and an eclipsed moon
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer, AnimationClip and NumberKeyframeTrack wing and thruster cycles; procedural movement, recoil and impact animation
sourceInformation.audio: Code-only Web Audio music, percussion, laser and impact effects, and formant-based gibberish voices; music defaults to 10%
sourceInformation.online: 1–2 player shared-world AI Hub co-op; standalone PeerJS WebRTC room codes; local simultaneous co-op
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium153 software WebGPU; full six-wave AI patrol; two full attract loops; keyboard, emulated standard gamepad, touch profile, live sliders, OfflineAudioContext; 2-page co-op and official AI Hub harness at150ms latency/50ms jitter/5% loss; render-free Rapier stress and WebGL visual checks. No physical controller or listener.
sourceInformation.research: Original Atari 2600 manual and AtariAge audiovisual notes; MobyGames mechanics and port descriptions; AI Hub protocol/client/harness; official Three.js and Rapier documentation

testingFeedback: 5 gameplay issues fixed; networking review identified 5 additional integration issues. Test-only expectation mistakes are excluded.
2 critical issues: an initial mouse click could be lost, and collider churn could crash the physics simulation.
The complete scripted six-wave patrol exposed the Rapier crash; repeated full attract loops verified the fix and replay behavior.
Headless software WebGPU screenshots were blank. State checks and WebGL compatibility screenshots supplied the useful evidence.
engineFeedback: Three.js native AnimationMixer clips and the scene graph made procedural winged characters and a layered ink illustration straightforward.
Rapier 0.19.3 reproduced an upstream collider-churn crash. Disabling CCD did not fix it; persistent physics-body pools did.
The combat rules, host-authoritative shared world, controller focus, procedural art and synthesized audio.
Diagnosing the Rapier broadphase failure and coordinating collision lifetimes with wave progression and network results.
none; application-level collider pooling avoids the version-specific issue without modifying engine source.
A first-party cel material with consistent WebGPU and WebGL behavior, plus clearer diagnostics for native physics failures.
promptFeedback: The specific source, controller-first direction and complete-demo requirement gave the design a clear identity.
The word Online supplied a library URL rather than defining whether standalone internet rooms were required; both were implemented.
Finishing and verifying standalone and AI Hub co-op within a single self-contained HTML artifact.
Define the minimum standalone network transport and clarify whether WebGL fallback is welcome on browsers without WebGPU.

aiHub.name: Demon Pecking Order
aiHub.description: Hold the moon against a flock of ink-winged troublemakers. Bend your shots, dash through volleys and scatter the sky across six waves and a vulnerable-core boss, solo or with a wingmate.
aiHub.controls: Left stick / A D / arrows: move; Cross / RT / Space / click: fire; Circle / Shift: dash; Square / L1 / Q: pulse; Options / Esc: pause; touch: drag, auto-fire, double-tap dash.
